title: NY State Assembly · District 58
area: Brooklyn: East Flatbush, Flatlands, Canarsie, and parts of Brownsville

context.text: Incumbent Monique Chandler-Waterman is unopposed in the general election. The Democratic and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were canceled and she advanced on both lines without appearing on the ballot. No Republican candidate filed.

summary.text: Monique Chandler-Waterman is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for Assembly District 58 in Brooklyn. A lifelong Brooklyn resident, she worked in community organizing, local nonprofit work and City Council outreach before winning a May 2022 special election to succeed N. Nick Perry. She was re-elected in 2022 and 2024 and is unopposed on the November 2026 ballot.

background.text: According to her official biography, she was born January 14, 1981, raised in East Flatbush, and is the daughter of Jamaican and Barbadian immigrants. Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as New York City.
She graduated from Boys and Girls High School, earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from Berkeley College, and received an MBA from Metropolitan College of New York.

Her official biography says she began organizing local block associations in 2005 and in 2008 co-founded a nonprofit providing academic, cultural, mental health and violence-prevention programs to families. Ballotpedia says she founded a day care center and co-founded the nonprofit East Flatbush Village, Inc.

Her official biography lists roles as Civilian Advisor for the NYPD's 67th Precinct, director of community outreach for then-City Council Member Jumaane Williams, and Outreach Director for New York City's Test & Trace Corps during the COVID-19 pandemic.
She won a May 2022 special election to succeed N. Nick Perry in the Assembly, after his appointment as U.S. Ambassador to Jamaica, and was re-elected in the 2022 and 2024 general elections.
For the 2025-2026 session she serves on the Banks, Children and Families, Election Law, Higher Education, Housing, and Mental Health committees.

Her official biography lists her as co-chair of the Anti-Gun Violence Subcommittee of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic and Asian Legislative Caucus and of the Mental Health Subcommittee of the Black Legislative Taskforce, and a participant in the Legislative Women's Caucus.

Honors named in her official biography include the New York City Council's Shirley Chisholm Woman of Distinction Award, the Caribbean Life Impact 40 Under 40 Award and the UFT School Safety Award. It says she lives in East Flatbush with her husband, Eric Waterman, and their four children.

priorities.text: "Truly affordable housing and policies that protect homeowners from predatory buyers."
"Quality public schools for all students throughout the district."

Police accountability, reflected in her sponsorship of numerous 2025-2026 bills addressing police body-worn cameras, duty-to-intervene requirements, racial profiling in traffic stops, and officer discipline.

positions.summary: Co-sponsor of the "Fair Share Act," which would authorize an additional 2% New York City income tax on residents, estates, and trusts with more than $1 million in annual taxable income.

record.text: Prime sponsor of A02084, establishing a state Office of Gun Violence Prevention and gun violence advisory council. Referred to the Codes Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A04735 ("Cariol's Law"), creating a duty for police and peace officers to intervene when they see another officer using excessive force. Amended twice and recommitted to the Codes Committee.

Prime sponsor of A07156, providing for indefinite suspension without pay of NYPD officers facing charges of incompetence or misconduct resulting in death or serious physical injury. Referred to the Governmental Employees Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07202, requiring police and peace officers executing a search warrant to wear an active, unobstructed body camera throughout the search. Referred to the Codes Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07225, assigning liability for monetary penalties from an illegal housing-unit conversion to the contractor and/or owner rather than the residents. Referred to the Cities Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.

Prime sponsor of A07181, defining racial profiling in traffic stops and directing a state study of the practice. Referred to the Governmental Operations Committee; has not advanced out of committee as of January 2026.
Serves on the Assembly's Banks, Children and Families, Election Law, Higher Education, Housing, and Mental Health committees for the 2025-2026 session.

researchNotes: Chandler-Waterman is unopposed on the Nov 3, 2026 ballot. She has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey in any cycle. Her campaign website (moniqueforny.com), used here for priorities, dates to her 2022 campaign and has not been updated with 2026-specific statements; her current legislative record (2025-2026 session), which is documented above, is the more up-to-date source for her priorities and positions. Chandler-Waterman's biography draws on her official Assembly biography and Ballotpedia; no independent news profile was used.
